                    ### Question
                    A thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus strain has been isolated at a retirement home. Many of the elderly had been infected with this strain and are experiencing shingles. Which of the following would be the best antiviral agent to treat this population?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Acyclovir
opb. Famciclovir
opc. Ganciclovir
opd. Cidofovir
ope. Amantadine

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
A thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus (VZV) strain is resistant to acyclovir, making it ineffective for treating shingles in this population. Famciclovir is an alternative antiviral that is effective against VZV and has better bioavailability, making it suitable for elderly patients. Ganciclovir is primarily used for cytomegalovirus (CMV) and is not effective for VZV. Cidofovir has some activity against VZV but is not first-line due to significant side effects. Therefore, famciclovir is the best choice for treating shingles in this elderly population infected with the thymidine kinase-deficient strain.
